title.en: Wednesday Addams Character Test

description.en: Try 18 original, harmless curiosity-cabinet and craft situations. Compare Wednesday, Enid, Bianca, Eugene, Morticia and Thing with all highest ties and six complete bilingual guides free. Unofficial fan edition, without plot trivia.
description.zh: 完成18道原创无害趣物柜与手作情境，比较星期三、伊妮德、比安卡、尤金、莫蒂西亚和小手。所有最高并列与六份双语全文免费。非官方同人版，不考剧情。

seoTitle.en: Wednesday Addams Character Test: Free Quiz & All 6 Results
seoTitle.zh: 《星期三》角色测试：免费作答与6种完整结果

introduction.en: Which Wednesday character do your creative hobby choices bring to mind? Imagine friends making an entirely original cabinet of paper curiosities: asking a precise question, welcoming visitors, setting fair challenges, noticing nature, shaping an atmosphere or making a practical action clear. This independent fan edition selects Wednesday, Enid, Bianca, Eugene, Morticia and Thing. All 18 situations and six complete guides are original and available free. No show knowledge, real investigation, animal handling or supernatural belief is needed.
introduction.zh: 创作爱好选择会让你想到《星期三》的哪位人物？想象朋友做完全原创纸趣物柜：具体提问、欢迎访客、设公平挑战、看自然、做气氛或让实际行动清楚。本独立同人版取星期三、伊妮德、比安卡、尤金、莫蒂西亚、小手。18情境和六份全文原创免费，不需剧情、真实调查、碰动物或超自然信念。

instructions.en: Think about a small optional craft or display activity you would enjoy now. Choose one of four responses in each situation, even if none fits perfectly. There is no correct answer or ranking of people’s worth. A character absent from an item is not rejected. Finish all 18 choices before counts appear; every highest tie receives a complete guide.
instructions.zh: 想象现在愿参加的小型可选手作、陈列活动，每情境四选一，即使都不完美。无正确答案，不排名人的价值；当题没出现者不算被拒绝。18题选完才出次数，每个最高并列都有全文。

title.zh: Netflix Tudum：《星期三》第一季人物与演员指南

title.en: Wednesday Addams
Enid Sinclair
Bianca Barclay
Eugene Ottinger
Morticia Addams

prompt.en: Friends are making an entirely original cabinet of harmless paper curiosities. What would you most enjoy first?
prompt.zh: 朋友做一个完全原创、无害的纸上趣物柜，你最喜欢先做什么？

label.en: Find one puzzling label and ask what its details actually support.
label.zh: 找一张有疑问的标签，问细节实际支持什么。

label.en: Choose a bright, welcoming introduction that makes the cabinet easy to approach.
label.zh: 选一个明亮友好介绍，让趣物柜好接近。

label.en: Propose a fair little challenge visitors can freely choose to try.
label.zh: 提一个访客能自由选试的公平小挑战。

label.en: Look closely at a fallen leaf’s ordinary shape for a nature-notebook page.
label.zh: 细看落叶普通形状，给自然笔记添一页。

prompt.en: A shy visitor is looking at the group’s handmade curiosity display. What appeals most?
prompt.zh: 一位拘谨访客在看手作趣物展，什么最吸引你？

label.en: Offer a cheerful invitation with a comfortable way to watch before joining.
label.zh: 愉快邀请，也给先看再加入的舒服办法。

label.en: Explain the optional challenge clearly so joining is a real choice.
label.zh: 讲清可选挑战，让参与真能自选。

label.en: Point out a small nature detail they might enjoy observing quietly.
label.zh: 指出一个可安静观察的小自然细节。

label.en: Show how the repeated colours and shapes give the display its own style.
label.zh: 展示重复色形怎样让陈列有自己的风格。

prompt.en: The group wants a playful contest beside its paper curiosities. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 小组想在纸趣物旁设个趣味竞赛，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Agree clear rules, equal turns and an easy way to decline the contest.
label.zh: 约清规则、平等轮次和容易拒绝的办法。

label.en: Make the activity about noticing ordinary natural details rather than collecting living things.
label.zh: 让活动看普通自然细节，不采集活物。

label.en: Give the contest a coherent visual theme that fits the rest of the cabinet.
label.zh: 给竞赛一致视觉主题，合柜子其他部分。

label.en: Prepare the small practical pieces people need for a turn.
label.zh: 备好每回合需要的小实际物件。

prompt.en: You can add one page to an original nature-and-curiosities notebook. What would you most enjoy?
prompt.zh: 原创自然趣物笔记能加一页，你最喜欢什么？

label.en: Observe a common fallen leaf or a photo and record a detail I had not noticed.
label.zh: 观察普通落叶或照片，记一个没注意过的细节。

label.en: Arrange the page so its shapes and tones belong to the notebook’s chosen style.
label.zh: 摆好页面形色，让它属于笔记选定风格。

label.en: Make a simple fold or tab that helps someone use the page.
label.zh: 做个简单折页、纸扣，让页面好用。

label.en: Ask what the page’s label can honestly claim from the observation.
label.zh: 问页面标签能据观察诚实说什么。

prompt.en: The cabinet contains many different paper objects. What would you prefer to contribute?
prompt.zh: 柜里有很多不同纸物件，你更愿意贡献什么？

label.en: A consistent arrangement that lets the collection have a distinctive atmosphere.
label.zh: 一致摆法，让收藏有独特气氛。

label.en: A small practical adjustment that makes the objects easier to handle.
label.zh: 一个小实际调整，让物件更好使用。

label.en: A careful question about an object whose explanation seems incomplete.
label.zh: 为解释不完整的物件提出仔细问题。

label.en: A friendly colourful cue that helps someone feel welcome to look.
label.zh: 一个友好彩色提示，让人愿意看。

prompt.en: A visitor cannot work out how to open a harmless paper compartment. What would you most like to do?
prompt.zh: 访客看不懂怎样开无害纸隔层，你最想做什么？

label.en: Offer a clear little demonstration or cue, then let them try.
label.zh: 给个清楚小演示或提示，再让对方试。

label.en: Inspect the explanation to see which step the wording leaves unclear.
label.zh: 看说明漏了哪步、哪里不清。

label.en: Make the invitation feel friendly rather than like a test they have failed.
label.zh: 让邀请友好，不像已经做错的考试。

label.en: Check that the activity’s rules give every visitor the same information.
label.zh: 核活动规则是否给每访客同样信息。

prompt.en: A fictional label on the cabinet claims more than the paper object shows. What appeals most?
prompt.zh: 趣物柜一张虚构标签说得比纸物件展示多，什么最吸引你？

label.en: Separate the observed detail from the extra story the group has invented.
label.zh: 分开实际细节与小组另外编的故事。

label.en: Rewrite the invitation so visitors can enjoy asking about it.
label.zh: 重写邀请，让访客好享受提问。

label.en: Turn the difference into a fair optional puzzle with a clear explanation afterwards.
label.zh: 把差别变公平可选谜题，之后给清楚解释。

label.en: Compare a similar ordinary natural pattern without disturbing any living creature.
label.zh: 比一个类似普通自然规律，不打扰活物。

prompt.en: Friends disagree over whether the cabinet should look dark or colourful. What would you enjoy?
prompt.zh: 朋友不同意趣物柜该暗色还是多彩，你喜欢什么？

label.en: Find a welcoming way to give both tastes a place in the display.
label.zh: 用友好办法，让两种喜好在陈列都有位置。

label.en: Agree a fair choice process without making one taste the winner as a person.
label.zh: 约公平选择方式，不把一种喜好等同人的胜利。

label.en: Look at ordinary natural colours for another source of inspiration.
label.zh: 看普通自然颜色，找另一个灵感来源。

label.en: Choose a deliberate shared style, with room for a few contrasting pieces.
label.zh: 有意识选共同风格，也容少量对比物件。

prompt.en: Someone proposes a challenge where experienced friends would have a large advantage. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 有人提的挑战对有经验朋友特别有利，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Adjust the rules so newcomers can choose a meaningful, fair way to participate.
label.zh: 改规则，让新人也能选有意义、公平的参与。

label.en: Use an observation task with familiar natural details rather than specialist knowledge.
label.zh: 用熟悉自然细节的观察任务，不考专门知识。

label.en: Keep the challenge’s presentation consistent with the cabinet’s atmosphere.
label.zh: 让挑战呈现仍与趣物柜气氛一致。

label.en: Prepare an example turn that makes the action easy to understand.
label.zh: 备一个样例回合，让动作好理解。

prompt.en: An ordinary leaf photo has an unexpectedly intricate pattern. What would you most enjoy?
prompt.zh: 普通叶片照片有意外复杂的纹路，你最喜欢什么？

label.en: Spend a little time noticing and recording the visible pattern itself.
label.zh: 花一点时间注意、记录可见纹路本身。

label.en: Use the pattern to develop the notebook’s recurring visual style.
label.zh: 用纹路发展笔记重复视觉风格。

label.en: Make a small movable frame that helps people compare parts of the photo.
label.zh: 做个可动小框，让人比较照片不同部分。

label.en: Ask which parts of our explanation come from the picture and which are guesses.
label.zh: 问解释哪部分来自照片、哪部分是猜想。

prompt.en: The group wants its collection to feel intentional without buying more things. What attracts you?
prompt.zh: 小组想不用再买东西，也让收藏有设计感，什么吸引你？

label.en: Repeat a few chosen shapes and tones across what we already have.
label.zh: 让已有物件重复几种选定形状、色调。

label.en: Rearrange one small fitting so the cabinet works more comfortably.
label.zh: 重摆一个小配件，让柜子用着更舒服。

label.en: Check whether each object’s label says something distinct and supportable.
label.zh: 核每物件标签是否有独特、可支持的内容。

label.en: Create a warm opening note that recognises the different makers.
label.zh: 做一张温暖开场卡，看见不同制作者。

prompt.en: A friend is explaining a foldable paper object but words are becoming confusing. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 朋友解释折纸物件，越说越乱，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Show one simple movement, with permission, and invite the friend to correct it.
label.zh: 经同意演示一个简单动作，邀请朋友修正。

label.en: Ask a precise question about the step that has two possible meanings.
label.zh: 对有两种意思的步骤提具体问题。

label.en: Keep the exchange light and welcoming while the friend tries again.
label.zh: 朋友重试时，让交流轻松友好。

label.en: Check that the demonstration would be available equally to everyone in the activity.
label.zh: 核活动里每人是否都同样有机会看演示。

prompt.en: The cabinet’s fictional story contains a curious contradiction. What would you most enjoy?
prompt.zh: 趣物柜虚构故事有个奇怪矛盾，你最喜欢什么？

label.en: Compare the details and ask whether the contradiction is intentional or needs editing.
label.zh: 比细节，问矛盾是故意设定，还是需编辑。

label.en: Make the question inviting enough that others want to explore it too.
label.zh: 让问题好接近，别人也想探索。

label.en: Offer a bounded puzzle round that gives everyone the same chance to examine it.
label.zh: 给一轮有范围谜题，让人人同样有机会看。

label.en: Look for a small natural observation that could inspire a harmless alternative explanation.
label.zh: 找个小自然观察，启发无害的替代解释。

prompt.en: Your cabinet-making group is welcoming someone with a different creative taste. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 趣物柜小组迎来一个创作喜好不同的人，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Invite them to show what they enjoy without first matching our mood.
label.zh: 邀对方展示喜欢什么，不用先配合我们气氛。

label.en: Make sure the group’s challenge and turn-taking rules remain fair to them.
label.zh: 让挑战、轮流规则对新人仍公平。

label.en: Find a shared ordinary observation that we can explore without needing the same taste.
label.zh: 找一个共同普通观察，不必喜好相同也能探索。

label.en: Discuss how their piece could sit within or beside the collection’s chosen style.
label.zh: 讨论对方作品怎样在选定风格之内或旁边出现。

prompt.en: The group is designing a friendly observation game for its handmade display. What appeals most?
prompt.zh: 小组给手作展设计友好观察游戏，什么最吸引你？

label.en: Clear challenge rules that reward participation without ranking people’s worth.
label.zh: 清楚挑战规则，重参与，不排名人的价值。

label.en: A small nature-photo detail that becomes interesting when you look twice.
label.zh: 一个多看一次就有趣的小自然照片细节。

label.en: A coherent visual motif that makes the game feel part of the collection.
label.zh: 一致视觉母题，让游戏属于整套收藏。

label.en: A practical demonstration piece that lets someone understand the move quickly.
label.zh: 一个实际演示件，让人快懂怎样动。

prompt.en: A nature-notebook page is interesting, but the explanation is becoming too certain. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 自然笔记页有趣，解释却越来越肯定，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Return to what we actually observed and leave the unknown parts open.
label.zh: 回到实际观察，未知部分先开放。

label.en: Keep the page’s visual atmosphere while simplifying the explanation.
label.zh: 简化解释，也保留页面视觉气氛。

label.en: Add a simple comparison tool that helps visitors look for themselves.
label.zh: 加一个简单比较工具，让访客自己看。

label.en: Ask exactly which claim needs more support before it is printed.
label.zh: 问印出来前，到底哪项主张还需支持。

prompt.en: Your collection needs a final page that belongs with the earlier ones. What would you enjoy?
prompt.zh: 收藏需一张与前页相属的末页，你喜欢什么？

label.en: Carry the chosen shapes, spacing and tone into a deliberate closing design.
label.zh: 把选定形状、间距、色调延续到收尾设计。

label.en: Make the page easy to open and return to its place.
label.zh: 让页面好开，也好回原位。

label.en: Check that the closing explanation follows the details shown earlier.
label.zh: 核收尾解释是否来自前面展示细节。

label.en: Offer a friendly closing invitation for visitors to share their own harmless idea.
label.zh: 友好收尾，邀访客分享自己的无害点子。

prompt.en: The handmade curiosity session is ending with one awkward little task. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 手作趣物活动快结束，剩一项别扭小任务，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Offer a specific practical action I am willing to do, with a clear finish.
label.zh: 给一项自己愿做、有明确终点的实际行动。

label.en: Ask what the task actually requires before anyone keeps guessing.
label.zh: 别再猜之前，问任务实际需要什么。

label.en: Make the closing exchange warm enough that people can say what help they want.
label.zh: 让收尾温暖，人们能说想要什么帮助。

label.en: Agree a fair way to share the remaining optional effort.
label.zh: 约一个公平办法，分余下可选投入。

title.en: Wednesday’s selected angle

paragraphs.en: Wednesday Addams is the central student named in Netflix’s Season 1 guide. This edition selects a precise question about a harmless paper curiosity. It does not treat quietness, dark aesthetics, emotion or analytical interest as signs of a disorder, superiority or danger. Enjoying a question can coexist with warmth and flexibility; no fictional line about emotions being weakness is adopted as advice or as a description of you.
paragraphs.zh: Netflix第一季指南的核心学生是星期三·亚当斯。本版选无害纸趣物里的具体提问，不把安静、暗色美学、情绪或分析兴趣当疾病、优越或危险迹象。喜欢提问可与温暖、弹性共存，不采用虚构“情绪是软弱”作建议或对你的描述。

title.en: A label that says too much

paragraphs.en: Friends make an original paper cabinet and write a fanciful label for one object. You ask which parts describe the object and which parts are invented. The group may keep the fanciful version if it is clearly presented as fiction. Your question makes that choice visible rather than exposing a person as wrong or requiring the hobby to become an investigation.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友做原创纸柜，为物件写幻想标签。你问哪部分描述物件、哪部分虚构；若清楚标虚构，可保留幻想版。提问让选择可见，不是揭穿人错，也不把爱好变调查。

title.en: Inquiry beside five other contributions

paragraphs.en: Enid offers a welcoming invitation and Bianca agrees a fair optional challenge. Eugene notices an ordinary natural detail, Morticia shapes a coherent atmosphere and Thing helps a practical action become clear. Wednesday’s selected angle asks what the explanation supports. These contributions can work together without ranking intelligence, emotional depth or who sees through other people. A tied count does not reveal a hidden diagnosis.
paragraphs.zh: 伊妮德友好邀请，比安卡约公平可选挑战；尤金看普通自然细节，莫蒂西亚做一致气氛，小手让实际动作清楚。星期三角度问解释支持什么。可合作，不排名智力、情绪深度或看穿人的能力，并列也不揭诊断。

title.en: A question should permit an answer

paragraphs.en: Decide what would answer the question before repeatedly reopening it. A playful cabinet can retain ambiguity when everyone understands its purpose. You can enjoy an atmosphere without proving every invented detail. A high count cannot establish obsession, emotional coldness or superior reasoning, and a lower count does not mean gullibility, shallow thinking or an inability to notice inconsistencies.
paragraphs.zh: 反复重提前，先想什么能回答。人人懂目的时，趣味柜可留模糊；不必证明每虚构细节才享受气氛。高计数不确立执念、情绪冷或推理更高，低计数不表示易骗、浅想或看不到不一致。

title.en: Try one bounded label question
title.zh: 试一个有范围的标签问题

paragraphs.en: Choose one label in a fictional craft project and separate observation, interpretation and invention in a few words. Ask the group whether that distinction improves the experience. Stop when the agreed question has an answer. This is feedback on an explanation, not an intelligence test, a clinical screen or permission to scrutinise real people’s private motives.
paragraphs.zh: 虚构手作选一标签，几句话分观察、解释、编造；问小组区分是否改善体验。约定问题答了就停。这反馈解释，不是智测、临床筛查，也不授权审视真人私密动机。

title.en: Original fan edition and source limits
title.zh: 原创同人版与来源边界

paragraphs.en: FermatMind independently authored this unofficial fan edition: original situations, mappings, examples and complete readings. Netflix Tudum’s Season 1 cast guide supports only basic character identities and limited fictional context; it does not validate these editorial angles or this bank. Names belong to their respective rights holders. No show images, dialogue, plot scenes, competitor questions or reports are reproduced. The comparison is entertainment without official affiliation, scientific validation or claims about diagnosis, emotional capacity, intelligence, dangerousness or supernatural power.
paragraphs.zh: 费马独立创作本非官方同人版的情境、映射、例子和全文。Netflix Tudum第一季人物指南只支持基本身份及有限虚构背景，不验证本版编辑角度、题本。名称属于各权利方；不复用剧照、台词、剧情场景、竞品题目或报告。本比较用于娱乐，无官方合作或科学验证，不推断诊断、情绪能力、智力、危险或超能力。

title.en: Enid’s selected angle

paragraphs.en: Netflix introduces Enid Sinclair as Wednesday’s roommate and identifies her colourful presence. This edition takes the narrow angle of a welcoming creative invitation. It does not measure extraversion, social intelligence, emotional health or a need for acceptance. A bright style can be optional and quiet; you do not have to remain cheerful, host every activity or make everybody comfortable to belong in a group.
paragraphs.zh: Netflix介绍伊妮德·辛克莱为星期三室友，也描述多彩呈现。本版窄取友好创作邀请，不测外向、社交智力、情绪健康或寻求接纳。明亮风格可安静、可选；不用永远开心、招待每次、照顾所有人舒服才属于群体。

title.en: A visitor may want to watch first

paragraphs.en: Someone pauses beside the handmade curiosity cabinet without touching anything. You offer a friendly opening and an equally acceptable chance to watch. A colourful cue can make the display easier to approach without requiring a conversation. The invitation works when the visitor can choose how much to engage, including choosing not to participate at all.
paragraphs.zh: 有人停在手作柜旁没动。你给友好开场，也容许旁观。彩色提示可让展好接近，不必要求交谈。邀请好用在访客能选参与多少，也能完全不参与。

paragraphs.en: Wednesday checks an explanation, Bianca clarifies fair challenge rules and Eugene observes a small natural detail. Morticia gives the collection a deliberate style while Thing shows a practical movement. Enid’s selected angle makes an opening for different visitors and tastes. These can coexist without ranking kindness, popularity or how much warmth a person should perform. A close count does not prescribe a social role.
paragraphs.zh: 星期三核解释，比安卡说公平规则，尤金看自然细节；莫蒂西亚做风格，小手演动作。伊妮德角度给不同访客、喜好入口。可共存，不排名善良、人气或该表演多少温暖；近分不规定社交角色。

title.en: Welcome includes a comfortable no

paragraphs.en: Notice whether an invitation is wanted and avoid treating someone’s quiet response as a problem to fix. Offer more than one way to join and keep your own effort voluntary too. A high count cannot establish people-pleasing, emotional sensitivity or exceptional sociability, while a lower count does not mean coldness, rejection of others or an inability to enjoy colourful company.
paragraphs.zh: 留意邀请是否被需要，别把安静反应当待修问题。给多种加入办法，自己投入也要自愿。高计数不确立讨好、情绪敏感或特别会社交，低计数不表示冷、拒绝人或不能享受多彩陪伴。

title.en: Try an invitation with a watching option

paragraphs.en: For a small optional display, write or say a short welcome that offers hands-on participation and a chance simply to look. Ask a willing visitor whether the choices were clear, then adjust the wording. You are testing an invitation in one setting, not measuring warmth, assessing friendship quality or deciding that you should always be the group’s cheerful host.

title.en: A newcomer can understand the first turn

paragraphs.en: Friends invent a small observation challenge for their paper display. Experienced makers know details that visitors have never seen, so you help give everyone the same starting information and an easy practice turn. People can decline or choose a noncompetitive version. Fairness here is a concrete arrangement, not a claim that one person has the authority to decide what is best for everyone.

title.en: A fair challenge beside five other contributions
title.zh: 公平挑战与另外五种贡献

paragraphs.en: Wednesday asks what the label supports, Enid makes the invitation friendly and Eugene notices a natural detail. Morticia gives the collection a visual thread while Thing demonstrates a useful action. Bianca’s selected angle helps an optional challenge work on agreed terms. These contributions can appear together without ranking ambition, confidence, influence or leadership ability. A high count cannot award a permanent place in charge.
paragraphs.zh: 星期三问标签支持，伊妮德友好邀请，尤金看自然细节；莫蒂西亚给视觉线索，小手演动作。比安卡角度让可选挑战按约运作。可并存，不排名抱负、自信、影响或领导；高计数不永久授予负责地位。

title.en: Winning is smaller than a person

paragraphs.en: Decide what the game is meant to reward and keep its result inside that activity. An experienced participant may prefer a different challenge rather than an advantage over a newcomer. A high count does not establish competitiveness, manipulation or superior fairness, and a lower count does not mean passivity, weakness or an inability to lead. People may simply prefer a different kind of voluntary play.
paragraphs.zh: 约游戏奖励什么，把结果留在活动内。有经验者可选不同挑战，不必占新人优势。高计数不确立好胜、操纵或更公平，低计数不表示被动、弱或不会带领，也许只是喜欢另一种自愿玩法。

title.en: Try one challenge with a real opt-out
title.zh: 试一个真能退出的挑战

paragraphs.en: For a harmless hobby game, explain one rule, offer a practice turn and include an equally welcome noncompetitive way to participate. Ask whether the participants understood the choices before starting. Afterwards, discuss the arrangement rather than ranking the people. This is feedback on game design, not a test of leadership, social influence or whether someone is naturally a winner.
paragraphs.zh: 无害爱好游戏说一条规则，给练习回合，也给同样欢迎的不竞赛参与。开始前问是否懂选择，之后聊安排而非排名人。这反馈游戏设计，不测领导、社交影响，也不决定谁天生赢家。

paragraphs.en: The official guide identifies Eugene Ottinger and his interest in bees. This edition translates that limited fictional context into looking at ordinary nature photographs or fallen leaves. It does not ask you to handle insects, disturb habitats or demonstrate scientific expertise. A preference for noticing a small pattern cannot establish intelligence, social naivety, courage or a special relationship with animals.

title.en: A leaf photo can be enough

paragraphs.en: The cabinet needs another notebook page, and you spend a little time with an ordinary leaf photograph. You record a shape or repeated line you had overlooked. The observation can be interesting without an exotic specimen or a dramatic explanation. You may leave the cause unknown and still share what is visible, keeping the activity modest, accessible and harmless.
paragraphs.zh: 柜子需笔记新页，你花一点时间看普通叶片照片，记漏看的形状、重复线。不需珍奇标本或戏剧解释也能有趣；原因可未知，仍分享可见内容，让活动小、易参与、无害。

title.en: Observation beside five other contributions

paragraphs.en: Wednesday asks which claim is supported, Enid offers a warm opening and Bianca agrees fair turns. Morticia shapes the notebook’s atmosphere while Thing makes a comparison tool usable. Eugene’s selected angle contributes an ordinary natural detail worth another look. These can work together without ranking curiosity, intelligence or whose interest is more serious. A tied reading does not create a scientific aptitude profile.
paragraphs.zh: 星期三问支持，伊妮德温暖开场，比安卡约公平轮次；莫蒂西亚做笔记气氛，小手让比较工具可用。尤金角度提供值得再看的普通自然细节。可合作，不排名好奇、智力或兴趣认真程度，并列不成科学潜能画像。

title.en: Observation and explanation are separate

paragraphs.en: Write down what you can actually see before naming a cause or a species. A photograph or common fallen material is enough for this hobby activity; there is no need to collect living creatures. A high count does not establish scientific talent or innocence, and a lower count does not mean incuriosity or disregard for nature. The quiz does not assess environmental behaviour or professional knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 说原因、物种前，先记真看见什么。照片、普通落下材料已够，不用采活物。高计数不确立科学天分、天真，低计数不表示不好奇、不在意自然；测验不评环境行为或专业知识。

title.en: Try a three-detail observation note

paragraphs.en: Choose a nature photograph you are allowed to view and record three visible details without searching for a grand explanation. Mark anything uncertain as unknown, then invite a friend to notice one additional feature. Compare the observations for interest, not a score. This is feedback on a small noticing activity, not proof of scientific ability, exceptional attention or a recommendation to work with animals.
paragraphs.zh: 选允许看的自然照片，不找宏大解释，记三个可见细节；不确定标未知，请朋友再看一项。为兴趣比较，不打分。这反馈小观察，不证明科学能力、注意超强，也不建议从事动物工作。

title.en: Use what is already in the cabinet

paragraphs.en: Friends want a collection to feel intentional without buying more objects. You repeat a few chosen tones, shapes or spaces across the pieces already made. The pattern gives visitors a visual thread while allowing a few contrasting contributions to stay distinct. A coherent collection does not require every maker to abandon their own taste or every object to tell exactly the same story.

title.en: Style beside five other contributions

paragraphs.en: Wednesday checks a label, Enid makes a welcome and Bianca sets fair optional rules. Eugene adds a small natural observation while Thing helps a paper object work. Morticia’s selected angle gives these pieces a deliberate visual relationship. These can coexist without ranking taste, emotional depth or who gives the group its identity. A close count does not decide how someone should dress, parent or live.
paragraphs.zh: 星期三核标签，伊妮德欢迎，比安卡设公平规则；尤金添自然观察，小手让纸物件好用。莫蒂西亚角度让各件有意识地视觉关联。可共存，不评品味、情绪深度或谁赋群体身份；近分不决定穿着、育儿、生活。

title.en: Consistency can leave room for contrast

paragraphs.en: Ask whether the collection’s style helps the people making and using it. A contrasting piece may make the arrangement richer rather than spoil it. Change the style when it stops serving the activity. A high count does not establish perfectionism, rigidity or refinement, and a lower count does not imply poor taste or a lack of care. There is no ideal aesthetic hidden in the score.
paragraphs.zh: 问风格是否服务制作者、使用者。对比件也许更丰富，不是破坏；不好用了就可改。高计数不确立完美主义、僵化或精致，低计数不表示品味差、不用心，分数没藏理想美学。

title.en: Try one visual thread and one exception
title.zh: 试一条视觉线索与一个例外

paragraphs.en: For a small collection, choose one repeated visual feature and deliberately keep one piece different. Ask a partner whether the arrangement is easier or more enjoyable to explore. Use that feedback to revise it without ranking anyone’s preferences. This is an experiment with a display, not a judgement of elegance, identity, purchasing power or the emotional meaning of a person’s aesthetic.
paragraphs.zh: 小收藏选一个重复视觉特征，再刻意留一件不同。问伙伴是否更好看、更好探索，按反馈改，不排名偏好。这试陈列，不评优雅、身份、购买力或个人美学的情绪意义。

paragraphs.en: Complete all 18 situations. Each explicitly mapped choice adds one raw count to one of six characters, making 18 counts in total. Every character appears 12 times, three times in each option position; an absent character is not rejected. All highest counts receive complete guides. All A gives three counts each and a six-way tie. The counts describe choices in this bank, not match percentages, norms, intelligence, empathy, competence or validated personality differences.
paragraphs.zh: 完成18个情境，每项明确映射的选择给六人物中的一位加一次原始计数，总计18次。每人物出现12次、每位置3次；没出现者不算被拒绝。所有最高都有全文；全选A每位3次，六方并列。次数仅描述本题本，不是匹配百分比、常模、智力、共情、能力或经验证人格差异。

title.en: Thing’s selected angle

paragraphs.en: Thing appears in the official guide as a character performed by Victor Dorobantu. This edition selects a clear practical action or demonstration in a voluntary craft activity. It does not compare bodies, assess disability, speech, dexterity or professional ability. Gestures, words, diagrams and assisted actions are equally possible ways to help. A character match never defines someone by a body part or assigns them a permanent supporting role.
paragraphs.zh: 官方指南列小手，由Victor Dorobantu表演。本版选自愿手作里的清楚实际行动、演示，不比较身体，不评残障、说话、灵巧或职业能力。手势、文字、图解、辅助动作都可帮忙；人物匹配不以部位定义人，也不永久分派辅助角色。

title.en: A demonstration can replace a confusing explanation

paragraphs.en: A friend’s foldable paper compartment is difficult to explain aloud. With permission, you show one movement or draw a cue, then let the friend correct the demonstration. The contribution is specific and reversible. It does not require touching another person’s work without asking, and it can stop after making this one action understandable rather than silently accepting every unfinished task.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友折纸隔层说不清。经同意，你演一个动作或画提示，让朋友修正。贡献具体、可逆，不用不问就动物件；让这一步清楚后可停，不悄悄接所有未完任务。

title.en: Practical help beside five other contributions
title.zh: 实际帮助与另外五种贡献

paragraphs.en: Wednesday asks a precise question, Enid offers a welcome and Bianca agrees fair turns. Eugene notices a small natural detail while Morticia gives the display a visual thread. Thing’s selected angle makes one action usable. These contributions can work together without ranking selflessness, usefulness, physical skill or who deserves recognition. A high count does not make you responsible for helping everyone.
paragraphs.zh: 星期三具体问，伊妮德欢迎，比安卡约公平轮次；尤金看自然细节，莫蒂西亚给视觉线索。小手角度让一项动作可用。可合作，不评无私、用处、身体技能或谁配认可；高计数不让你负责帮所有人。

title.en: Useful help has a chosen boundary

paragraphs.en: Ask what help is wanted and choose what you can comfortably offer. A demonstration may be unnecessary, or another format may work better for the person using it. Your contribution can be visible and acknowledged rather than assumed. A high count cannot establish obedience, exceptional dexterity or lack of personal needs; a lower count does not mean selfishness or an inability to contribute practically.
paragraphs.zh: 问需要什么，选舒服能给的。也许不用演示，或另一形式更适合。贡献可被看见、认可，不是理所当然。高计数不确立服从、特别灵巧或没个人需要，低计数不表示自私、不能实际贡献。

title.en: Try one requested action with a finish
title.zh: 试一项被需要、有终点的行动

paragraphs.en: For an optional craft task, ask a partner which single step would be useful to clarify. Agree on a demonstration, diagram or short description, then let them try the step in their preferred way. Stop after the agreed check. You are testing one form of practical help, not measuring motor skills, communication capacity or how much service a person owes their friends.
paragraphs.zh: 可选手作问伙伴哪一步想弄清，约演示、图或短描述，再让按喜欢方式试；约定核完就停。检验实际帮助形式，不测动作技能、沟通能力，也不衡量欠朋友多少服务。

answer.en: No. Creative hobby choices cannot establish emotional capacity, diagnosis, trauma, IQ, empathy, dangerousness, bodily ability or powers. Dark and bright tastes are not health labels. These are selective editorial comparisons, with no character’s harm, authority or family role assigned to you.
